en.r: Floresta Petrificada National Park is a national park in Arizona, United States. It covers 380 km² and has been protected since 1962. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
en.h: Indigenous peoples lived here for over 13,000 years, leaving petroglyphs and ruins such as Puerco Pueblo. Looting of petrified wood led to a national monument in 1906 and a national park on 9 December 1962. Route 66 crossed the area.
en.ff: Large deposits of Triassic petrified wood over 200 million years old, plus fossils of early reptiles and dinosaurs. To the north begin the colorful badlands of the Painted Desert.

en.r: Saguaro National Park is a national park in Arizona, United States. It covers 374 km² and has been protected since 1994. It is managed by the U.S. National Park Service. Under the IUCN system it is category II, the national park category: it protects whole ecosystems and welcomes visitors.
